gloss: patronage; personal backing; favor — especially the support a customer or superior gives to a shop, performer, or junior person (often used in business and theatrical contexts)

definitions.gloss: patronage; personal backing; favor — the support, recommendation, or preferential treatment that a customer, superior, or established person gives to a shop, performer, junior, etc.
definitions.explanation: The noun form of {引|ひ}き{立|た}てる ("to favor / support / recommend"). It refers to the act of singling someone or something out for support — patronizing a particular shop, repeatedly recommending a junior employee, or championing a young performer. {引|ひ}き{立|た}て almost always appears with the honorific お (お{引|ひ}き{立|た}て) in a phrase the speaker addresses to a customer or benefactor, expressing gratitude for the addressee's continued support. The implication is that the speaker has been the beneficiary of the addressee's generosity.

examples.japanese: お{引|ひ}き{立|た}てを{賜|たまわ}る。
examples.english: To receive your patronage. (formal letter phrase)

examples.japanese: {日頃|ひごろ}より{格別|かくべつ}のお{引|ひ}き{立|た}てを{頂|いただ}き、ありがとうございます。
examples.english: Thank you for the special patronage you regularly extend to us.

examples.japanese: {今後|こんご}とも{変|か}わらぬお{引|ひ}き{立|た}てのほど、よろしくお{願|ねが}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。
examples.english: We humbly ask for your continued, unchanging patronage going forward.

examples.japanese: {師匠|ししょう}のお{引|ひ}き{立|た}てがあって、{若手|わかて}{役者|やくしゃ}は{大|おお}きな{役|やく}をもらうことができた。
examples.english: Thanks to his master's patronage, the young actor was able to land a major role.

notes:
{引|ひ}き{立|た}て is the noun form of the verb {引|ひ}き{立|た}てる ("to favor / single out for support"). It refers to the patronage, backing, or active support that a customer, superior, or established figure shows toward a shop, junior, or younger artist. It is almost always used with the honorific お — お{引|ひ}き{立|た}て.

WHO/WHAT IT REFERS TO:
- The actions of a benefactor (customer, superior, master) toward the speaker or speaker's organization
- The speaker is the beneficiary, not the giver
- Cannot describe one's own act of supporting someone — for that, use {引|ひ}き{立|た}てる as a verb

FIXED PHRASES (BUSINESS / SHOP CONTEXT):
- {日頃|ひごろ}より{格別|かくべつ}のお{引|ひ}き{立|た}てを{賜|たまわ}り、ありがとうございます。 — Thank you for your special patronage as always.
- {今後|こんご}とも{変|か}わらぬお{引|ひ}き{立|た}てのほど、よろしくお{願|ねが}い{申|もう}し{上|あ}げます。 — We humbly ask for your continued patronage.
- {皆様|みなさま}のお{引|ひ}き{立|た}てに{支|ささ}えられて、{当店|とうてん}は{創業|そうぎょう}{五十年|ごじゅうねん}を{迎|むか}えることができました。 — Sustained by all of your patronage, our shop has reached its fiftieth anniversary.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{引|ひ}き{立|た}てを{賜|たまわ}る: to receive (your) patronage (very formal)
- お{引|ひ}き{立|た}てを{頂|いただ}く: to receive (your) patronage
- お{引|ひ}き{立|た}てに{あずかる}: to be the beneficiary of patronage
- {格別|かくべつ}のお{引|ひ}き{立|た}て: special / extraordinary patronage
- {変|か}わらぬお{引|ひ}き{立|た}て: continuing / unchanging patronage
- {師匠|ししょう}の{引|ひ}き{立|た}て: a master's patronage (theater / arts world)
- {上司|じょうし}の{引|ひ}き{立|た}て: a superior's backing (workplace)

CONTEXTS OF USE:
- Shops/businesses to customers: appears in greeting cards, year-end letters, opening of business correspondence
- Theater / traditional arts ({歌舞伎|かぶき}, {落語|らくご}): a master singling out a junior for advancement
- Workplace: a senior promoting or recommending a junior employee for opportunities

SIMILAR / RELATED TERMS:
- ご{愛顧|あいこ}: (your) patronage — very common in retail business letters; near synonym
- ご{高配|こうはい}: (your) kind consideration — broader, more abstract
- ご{支援|しえん}: (your) support — neutral and broader; less archaic
- ご{厚情|こうじょう}: (your) deep goodwill — focuses on warm feelings
- {引|ひ}き{立|た}てる: the source verb — to favor / single out / make stand out
- {挽|ひ}きたて: (homophone) freshly ground (e.g., coffee beans) — completely unrelated meaning

REGISTER:
- Formal — appropriate for business letters, ceremonial speeches, theater-world contexts
- Always honorific in reference (お~)
- Inappropriate in casual conversation
